etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English replyen, replien, borrowed from Old French replier (“to reply”), from the Latin replicō, replicāre (“I fold back”) (in Late or Medieval Latin "to reply, repeat"), from re + plicō (“I fold”); the noun derives from the verb by nominalisation. Doublet of replicate and replica.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To give a written or spoken response, especially to a question, request, accusation or criticism; to answer.
(intransitive) To act or gesture in response.

quote.citation: 1988, Emmanuel Doe Ziorklui, Ghana: Nkrumah to Rawlings:
quote.text: It is a sound to be dreaded until you ascertain that it is being made by friendly forces; even then, your welcome to it must be tempered with some caution, because gunfire usually leads to replying gunfire […]
[…]  bulged the onion bag for the Blades, and Downes and Prendergast replied for the Owls.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To repeat something back; to echo.
A written or spoken response; part of a conversation.
(US, law) A document written by a party specifically replying to a responsive declaration and in some cases an answer.
